headline: Nuggets beat the Pacers 114-102 in Mexico City behind Nikola Jokic's 19 points
text: MEXICO CITY -- — Nikola Jokic scored 10 of his 19 points in the first quarter and the Denver Nuggets beat the Indiana Pacers 114-102 in Mexico City. Jokic also grabbed 13 rebounds and dished out eight assists, while Cameron Johnson added 18 points and Jamal Murray finished with 16 for the Nuggets, who have won four of their last five games. “I just try to play the game the right way, hopefully we can win more games; to win is the most important thing, I do not think about stats,” Jokic said. Pascal Siakam scored 23 points and Larry Nance Jr . added 15 off the bench for the Pacers, who were the home team in the NBA’s 35th game played south of the border. Indiana has lost five of its last six games. The Pacers played without All-Star guard Tyrese Haliburton , who missed the trip due to a hamstring strain. Denver capitalized on a four-minute Indiana scoring drought in the second quarter with a 15-0 run. Murray's jumper extended the Nuggets’ lead to 64-37 — their largest of the game — with less than a minute remaining in the first half. “It was tough environment, we are not used to this, the altitude and everything is hard to get going,” Siakam said. “Our force and energy was better in the second half, but it was not enough.” The Pacers responded in the third quarter, pulling closer following back-to-back 3-pointers from Aaron Nesmith that cut the score to 79-67. A layup by Quenton Jackson with 1:16 left in the quarter further trimmed Denver’s lead to 10. Jarace Walker hit a 3-pointer that brought Indiana within 102-95 with 7:26 left to play, but the Nuggets answered with six straight points to restore a double-digit lead and secure the win. The game marked the 35th NBA appearance in the country since the league first brought exhibition games to Mexico in 1992. No country outside the United States and Canada has hosted more. Of those 34 previous matchups, 15 were regular-season games, and the last 12 — including Saturday’s tilt between Indiana and Denver — sold out. “The energy was awesome, I got to admit that there is an atmosphere to this building, when we got out on the court you could feel the juice, and the energy,” said Nuggets coach David Adelman. “The NBA is global and it belongs here too.” Up next Nuggets: At Houston on Monday night. Pacers: At Dallas on Monday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jalen Johnson scores 30 points in his return as Hawks make 4th-quarter charge to beat Nets 124-121
text: ATLANTA -- — Nickeil Alexander-Walker sank two free throws with 1:26 remaining to give Atlanta its first lead and the Hawks recovered from a big early deficit to beat the Brooklyn Nets 124-121 on Saturday night. Jalen Johnson led Atlanta with 30 points in his return after missing three games with a left ankle sprain. Alexander-Walker and Aaron Wiggins each added 20 as the Hawks, who trailed by 17 points in the first quarter, earned their fourth consecutive win. The Nets were denied in their attempt for back-to-back wins for the first time this season. Atlanta outscored Brooklyn 36-26 in the final period. Michael Porter Jr . scored 25 points and Nolan Traore added a season-high 19. Julius Randle also had 19 for Brooklyn. Danny Wolf sank a 3-pointer with 1.5 seconds remaining to trim Atlanta's lead to two points. The Hawks called a timeout and Onyeka Okongwu , who had 16 points, sealed the win by sinking one of two free throws. The hot-shooting Nets took an early 31-14 lead but led only 70-66 at halftime and saw their advantage trimmed to one point four times in the fourth quarter, including at 114-113 before the Hawks finally completed their comeback. Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr . scored 18 points, including three 3-pointers in the fourth quarter. The Nets lost six of their first seven games before beat Charlotte 114-104 on Wednesday night and then launching a four-game trip by beating the Hawks. Day'Ron Sharpe had 12 points, 13 assists and 10 rebounds for hist first career triple-double. Nets coach Jordi Fernandez said guard Egor Demin , who started the first four games before missing five games with a bone bruise in his right leg, will miss at least one more game “and then we'll go from there.” Up next Nets: At Dallas on Sunday night. Hawks: Host Los Angeles Lakers on Monday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jalen Brunson scores 31 to power Knicks past Cavs 109-97 in rematch of last year's Eastern finalists
text: CLEVELAND -- — Jalen Brunson scored 31 points, Karl-Anthony Towns added 29 and the New York Knicks made big plays when they needed them in a 109-97 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Saturday night in a rematch between last year's Eastern Conference finalists. Brunson scored 18 straight in the second quarter to help the defending NBA champions take control. He added nine assists and drained a crucial jumper in the final three minutes as the Knicks held off Cleveland's comeback. Donovan Mitchell scored 21 of his season-high 37 points in the fourth quarter for the Cavs, who handed Philadelphia its first road loss on Friday. It was the first meeting between New York and Cleveland since last season's conference finals, which the Knicks swept. They blew out the Cavs by 37 in Game 4 on their Rocket Arena home floor. Before that game, Cavs coach Kenny Atkinson drew criticism for saying his team was “analytically" winning the series. Six months later, Atkinson tried to clarify his remarks, saying in no way was he implying the Knicks weren't better. “They dominated it, and they did it again against San Antonio (in the Finals),” he said. Brunson, the MVP of last year's Finals, went on a one-man scoring spree in the second. With Cleveland up 39-37, Brunson made a 3-pointer and then reeled off 18 in a row over a span of 4:24 to put the Knicks ahead 52-45. On New York's next possession, Brunson had his shot blocked but he grabbed a loose ball and fed Landry Shamet for a 3 to put the Knicks up by 10. Knicks guard Josh Hart missed his second straight game with an ankle injury that coach Mike Brown said is “nothing major.” The Cavs were without center Jarrett Allen (knee) and guards Jaylon Tyson (ankle) and Sam Merrill (elbow). Up next Knicks: Host Milwaukee on Tuesday. Cavaliers: At Charlotte on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Thunder rout the poor-shooting Wizards 114-75
text: OKLAHOMA CITY -- — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 30 points in three quarters and the Oklahoma City Thunder routed poor-shooting Washington 114-75 on Saturday night, holding the Wizards to the lowest total in the NBA this season. Jared McCain added 19 points, and rookie Aday Mara had 18 points, eight rebounds and three blocks for Oklahoma City (8-2), which has won five of seven games since losing starters Jalen Williams , Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren to long-term injuries. Rookie AJ Dybantsa scored 19 points and Alex Sarr had 15 points and 14 rebounds for Washington (4-6), which played without big man Anthony Davis . The Wizards made 29 of 98 shots (29.6%) and made only 7 of 43 3-point attempts. The Wizards have lost three straight. Both teams played NBA Cup games the previous night, but it didn't appear to affect Oklahoma City, which shot 50% in the first half and built a 57-36 lead behind 17 points from McCain and 16 from Gilgeous-Alexander, who sat out the fourth quarter. Washington missed its first seven field goal attempts on the way to 15-for-52 shooting (28.8%) for the half. Trey Young, who starred at nearby Norman High and the University of Oklahoma, was held to one field goal in six attempts and finished with four points. Oklahoma City took a 76-54 lead on a 3-point shot by Gilgeous-Alexander with 4:38 left in the third quarter. A 3 by rookie Bennett Stirtz gave the Thunder a 90-59 lead after three quarters. The advantage grew to 109-69 on a basket by newcomer Micah Peavy . Hall of Famer Allen Iverson, in town for a birthday party, sat courtside. Up next Wizards: At Detroit on Monday night. Thunder: At Portland on Tuesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Stephen Curry scores 41 points as Warriors win seventh straight, beating Magic 126-119 in overtime
text: SAN FRANCISCO -- — Stephen Curry converted a three-point play with 1:38 left in overtime that put Golden State ahead then scored a layup in the final minute to finish with 41 points, six rebounds and six assists, and the Warriors held off the Orlando Magic 126-119 on Saturday night for their seventh straight win. Wendell Carter Jr . missed two free throws with 1:15 remaining that would have tied the game before Curry came through again. Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg made a key 3-pointer in overtime and contributed 23 points and eight rebounds. A day earlier he shared a video of gifting his mother a home in California. Golden State started 0-3 and now has its longest winning streak since seven in a row from March 3-15, 2025. Franz Wagner had 30 points and 11 assists and Tristan da Silva and Carter each scored 19 for the Magic, who have lost four straight on the Warriors’ home floor. Brandin Podziemski scored 15 points and Draymond Green had a season-high 13 assists for Golden State. The final minutes of regulation were a back-and-forth scoring frenzy. Curry made a go-ahead layup with 25.2 seconds left and Jamal Cain 's putback with 2 seconds left on Orlando's third try in the final moments sent it into overtime. Cain had 18 points and 12 rebounds off the bench to help rally the Magic, who trailed 57-41 at halftime then led 78-77 going into the final period. Curry recorded his second 40-point game this season and fourth in the last five with at least 30 points. It was his 16th 40-point effort after age 35, most in NBA history. LeBron James has 15 and Michael Jordan did it 12 times. The 38-year-old Curry, in his 18th season, also became the seventh player ever with 26,000 points, 5,000 rebounds and 6,000 assists, according to ELIAS. Georges Niang and Carter received double technicals at the 9:17 mark of the second quarter when they tussled after Niang grabbed the Orlando center in the paint. Security guards kept Green from getting involved following his ejection against Phoenix last Monday. Niang notched his third straight double-digit scoring game with 11 points. Up next Magic: At Sacramento on Tuesday night. Warriors: Host Charlotte on Monday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Booker scores 24, Suns outlast Rockets 102-99 for 1st back-to-back wins of season
text: PHOENIX -- — Devin Booker scored 24 points, including seven straight to break a late tie, and the Phoenix Suns held off the Houston Rockets 102-99 on Saturday night. Booker broke a 95-all tie with a basket with just under 4 minutes left, then hit a 3-pointer to make it 100-95. Another basket with 2:30 left made it a seven-point Phoenix lead, and Houston couldn't come back. Former Sun Kevin Durant missed a 3-point attempt in the final seconds and Phoenix ran out the clock. Jalen Green had 16 points, Miles Bridges had 13 points and 10 rebounds and Dillon Brooks scored 11 for the Suns, who snapped an eight-game losing streak against the Rockets. With their victory over Orlando on Thursday night, the Suns have won consecutive games for the first time this season. Durant led the Rockets with 21 points and 10 rebounds. Amen Thompson scored 17 points, Fred VanVleet had 16, and Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Sengun added 15 apiece. The Suns shot 76% (16 of 21) in the first quarter in building a 35-23 lead. They led by 19 in the second quarter but Houston finished on a 22-3 run to tie it at 47 at halftime. Phoenix was 4 of 19 from the field in the quarter. VanVleet’s jumper tied it with under a minute to go before the break. He had 10 points in the period and 13 for the half. Khaman Maluach had 11 points off the bench to lead the Suns before halftime. Booker played in his 745th career game on Saturday, passing Steve Nash for third place in Suns history. Up next Rockets: Host Denver on Monday night. Suns: Host San Antonio on Monday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Victor Wembanyama scores 29 points in Spurs win over Blazers
text: PORTLAND, Ore -- — Victor Wembanyama scored 29 points and led the San Antonio Spurs to a 125-103 blowout win over the Portland Trail Blazers on Saturday night. Devin Vassell added 15 points for the Spurs (8-2) along with 14 each from Stephon Castle and Julian Champagnie , and 13 from Dylan Harper . Deni Avdija led the Blazers (6-3) with 15 points. Scoot Henderson added 13 points, along with 12 from Damian Lillard and 11 from Jrue Holiday off the bench. Yang Hansen had his first career double-double with 12 points and 10 rebounds. Wembanyama’s 29 points came in just 24 minutes, and he took just 13 shots, going 9 of 13 from the field and 3 of 6 from 3-point range. Up next Spurs: At Phoenix on Monday. Trail Blazers: Host back-to-back matchups against Oklahoma City on Tuesday and Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
